metrics.n: Tableau Semantics centralizes metrics, calculations, and definitions in a governed layer. Exact stage not shown on pages I could open.

dimensions.n: Unverified: no page I could open describes dimensions, hierarchies, or time grains in Tableau Semantics.

relationships.n: Per Tableau MCP docs quoted by Hex, the semantic model defines how tables relate and how KPIs are calculated.

synonyms.n: Same quoted docs say the model maps business terminology to fields. Field-level synonym settings not confirmed.

verifiedQueries.n: Q&A Calibration is Beta or Pilot per Hex. Not confirmed as question-to-SQL pairs.

nl2sql.n: Concierge Analytics Q&A runs natural-language questions over semantic models; April 2026 notes list its scope controls as GA.

ontology.n: No ontology object found. Semantic models sit on Data 360 objects (DMO, DLO, CIO).

vector.n: Unverified: no vector search on data found in sources opened.

mcp.n: April 2026 release notes say Tableau Next MCP is GA. The tool reference page is still titled Beta.

governance.n: April 2026 Concierge update lets admins govern agent data access by defining specific semantic models.

openStandard.n: Ossie converters repo has a Salesforce directory but no Tableau directory. Tableau appears only as an example export target.

offers: Tableau Next MCP server (GA Apr 2026) lets agents query semantic models, browse assets, and ask Analytics Agent questions.
Open-source tableau-mcp works with Tableau Cloud and Server, hosted or self-hosted.
Semantic Model Scope in Concierge limits which semantic models an agent may use.
Data layer runs on Data 360 with zero-copy links to Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, and Databricks.
gaps: I could not open Tableau or Salesforce docs, so dimension, synonym, and verified-query features are not confirmed.
Q&A Calibration and Auto Semantic Model Creation are Beta or Pilot.
Semantic layer lives in Salesforce Data 360. Hex argues trust and logic sit inside one vendor cloud.
No Tableau converter in the Ossie repo.
vendors.nl2sqlPath: Build a semantic data model in Tableau Next on Data 360, then use Concierge or the Tableau Next MCP server to ask questions. Calls go through the semantic model, so the agent does not write raw SQL. Check the Salesforce MCP docs for the current GA tool list.

openToOtherTools.n: Tableau Next MCP is GA (Apr 2026). Open-source tableau-mcp is also available. No SQL interface or OSI export found.

Spotter (AI analyst, replaced Sage and Ask Sage)

dimensions.n: Unverified: I could not open the Models docs to confirm dimension or time-grain objects.

relationships.n: Unverified: join definition in Models not confirmed from pages opened.

synonyms.n: Unverified. Docs list "Generate AI Synonyms at the model level" as removed in 26.6.0.cl; other synonym fields not confirmed.

vendors.name: Metabase
vendors.tagline: Open-source BI with a Library semantic layer, Metabot AI, and an official MCP server.
vendors.verdictNote: Library metrics, measures, segments, and glossary feed Metabot and a permission-scoped MCP server, but no joins or verified query pairs are documented.

artifacts.name: Library (published tables, metrics, SQL snippets, Glossary)
Glossary (business terms for people and agents)

metrics.n: Library metrics are standardized calculations that rank first in navigation, search, and the query builder.

dimensions.n: No dimension or time-grain object found in docs. Segments are saved filters only.

relationships.n: Published-tables doc defines no joins. It only says related tables are published together.

synonyms.n: Glossary terms help Metabot understand your terminology. Table and metric descriptions exist; how Metabot uses them is not stated.

verifiedQueries.n: No question-to-SQL pairs. Metabot can be limited to verified or Library content only.

nl2sql.n: Metabot generates SQL but does not run it. Its search is limited to tables, metrics, questions, models, and dashboards.

vector.n: No vector search on data found in sources opened.

mcp.n: Official server in Metabase 60 (Apr 2026), upgraded in 64 (Oct 2026). Admin enables it. Needs AI features on.

governance.n: MCP and OAuth scopes follow the connecting user permissions. Pro and Enterprise can limit tools per group.

openStandard.n: Library syncs to Git. No Metabase directory in the Ossie converters repo listing I fetched.

offers: Library holds curated tables, metrics, and SQL snippets; admins can limit Metabot to Library content.
Measures give one official formula per table, for example Net Promoter Score.
Official MCP server needs no AI provider in Metabase. The client supplies the model.
Library, measures, segments, and glossary sync to Git when Library sync is on.
MCP also offers raw SQL, which admins can turn off.
gaps: Measures only work on questions that query the measure table directly. No joins or nested queries.
Metabot checks only the first 100 tables when no table is named, and may invent tables beyond that.
No synonyms field or verified question-SQL pairs found; the Glossary is the main text context.
Metabot cannot find segments, measures, documents, or collections on its own.
MCP tool access controls and analytics need Pro or Enterprise.
vendors.nl2sqlPath: Publish clean tables to the Library, add metrics, measures, and glossary terms, then set Metabot to curated content only. For your own agent, enable the MCP server and let the client supply the model. Keep a warehouse semantic layer if you need joins or synonyms.

openToOtherTools.n: Official MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.0) searches and queries metrics and tables within user permissions. No OSI export.

vendors.name: Apache Superset
vendors.tagline: Open-source BI with datasets, an MCP service, and a semantic layer feature still behind a flag.
vendors.verdictNote: Datasets act as a light semantic layer and an MCP server exists, but external semantic layers are behind a default-off flag and no first-party NL-to-SQL was found.

artifacts.name: Datasets (lightweight semantic layer: metrics and dimensions)
Semantic Layers (external layers as a datasource type, SIP-182)

metrics.n: The Superset README describes a lightweight semantic layer for defining metrics and dimensions on datasets.

dimensions.n: Same README line covers dimensions. Hierarchy and time-grain objects not confirmed; SIP-182 thread asks for hierarchies.

relationships.n: Unverified: datasets declaring joins not confirmed from pages opened.

synonyms.n: Unverified: no synonym field confirmed in sources opened.

verifiedQueries.n: No verified question-SQL pairs found. MCP can save SQL queries.

nl2sql.n: No first-party NL-to-SQL found in sources opened. Teams use MCP clients.

mcp.n: MCP docs list tools for datasets, charts, dashboards, and SQL. The page gives no maturity label, so stage is unconfirmed.

governance.n: MCP RBAC is on by default, so each tool checks the caller Superset permissions. Actions are logged.

openStandard.n: SIP-182 vote approved Jun 22, 2026. It names Cube, MetricFlow, Snowflake semantic views, and OSI. No Superset converter listed.

offers: Built-in MCP server (superset mcp run) has tools such as list_datasets, query_dataset, execute_sql, and generate_chart.
MCP supports JWT auth and per-tool RBAC; admins can disable tools.
SIP-182 plans first-class external semantic layers (MetricFlow, Cube, Snowflake semantic views).
Apache-2.0 licence, self-hosted.
gaps: SEMANTIC_LAYERS defaults to False. Preset says it targets Superset 7.0; the 6.1 docs list it as a flag, so release is unclear.
SIP-182 backends are experimental examples, not a confirmed supported list.
MCP docs give no GA or Preview label. Needs Superset 5.0 or later, Python 3.11 or later, and fastmcp.
No first-party NL-to-SQL, synonym, or verified-query feature was found.
vendors.nl2sqlPath: Define metrics and dimensions on datasets and run the built-in MCP service so your agent calls dataset tools. For governed metrics, wait for the semantic layers flag to settle or keep metrics in Cube or dbt.

snippet.title: Start the Superset MCP server (from the MCP server doc)
snippet.code:
superset mcp run --host 127.0.0.1 --port 5008
# endpoint: /mcp
# MCP_AUTH_ENABLED = True enables JWT auth
# MCP_RBAC_ENABLED = True is the default

openToOtherTools.n: MCP service with dataset and SQL tools and JWT auth. Docs show no maturity label. No OSI export.

notes.text: WebFetch could reach only GitHub pages in this session. Vendor sites (Tableau, Salesforce, ThoughtSpot, Sigma, Domo, Metabase.com, Superset.apache.org) failed to connect, and the search budget ran out. Claims for those vendors come from search result text. Items I could not check are marked Unverified or set to level 0 with a note.

ThoughtSpot Worksheets were deprecated Nov 2024 and removed Aug 2025, with content moved to Models. Sage and Ask Sage were removed Dec 2025 and replaced by Spotter. Ask Sigma became Sigma Assistant in Apr 2026.
April 2026 release notes say Tableau Next MCP is GA, but the Salesforce tool reference page is titled Beta. Treat the exact GA tool list as unconfirmed.

sources.t: Tableau Next MCP Beta Server Tool Reference

notes.text: Announced Mar 12, 2026 as an agentic semantic layer with a metrics catalog and an OSI alignment claim. Only the press release and reprints were seen. The Ossie converters repo does list a thoughtspot directory.
Domo lists its Semantic Layer on a Beta Features page, and the Sep 2026 release notes list Semantic View Integration as beta. Analysts say the AI Library and MCP expansion are beta too.

MCP server arrived in Metabase 60 (Apr 2026) and was upgraded in Metabase 64 (Oct 2026, date from a directory listing, not Metabase). The client supplies the model, so no Metabase AI provider is needed. Metabot and MCP are included in every plan per Metabase AI page snippets.
The 6.1.0 feature flag page lists SEMANTIC_LAYERS, default off. A Preset post says it is on master and targeted at 7.0. I could not settle which release ships it.

Tableau Semantics stage and dimensions, Tableau Pulse, ThoughtSpot MCP stage and Models details, Sigma Snowflake Semantic Views integration, Domo and Superset data platform lists, Superset MCP maturity, and Metabase 64 date.
